newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK DEBT GETS THUMBS UP FROM MERRILL LYNCH.
newsitem.headline: GREEK DEBT GETS THUMBS UP FROM MERRILL LYNCH.

text.p: Merrill Lynch expected a weaker mark and falling German bond yields to benefit Greek debt in the next 12-months but was negative on Greek equities.

"Greek financial assets will benefit from a weaker mark which provides positive support for U.S bond prices," said Johnson who called Greece an attractive emerging market debt story," its senior international investment strategist Douglas Clark Johnson told Money Show participants on Saturday.
"Greece tends to outperform when mark bond yields fall," he said.
But Johnson was bearish on Greek equities for the next year pointing to an upward trending dividend payout ratio and a negative risk-return profile.

According to a diagramme he presented at the meeting the Athens bourse enjoyed a low return, somewhere between 14 and 12 percent in the last few years, and a high risk measured as the standard deviation of returns in the 61 to 65 percent bracket.

Asked whether the frequent revamping of Greece's benchmark stock index over the last few years rendered the risk and return measures unreliable, Johnson pointed to the need to incorporate as much past price data as possible implying that treatment of structural breaks would not alter the results.
The Merril Lynch strategist added that his house was negative to neutral for emerging Europe.
Yet Merril Lynch's stochastic indicator flashed a major buy signal in the September-October period but the firm did not respond citing a poor fundamental backdrop.
He pointed to a lack of equity culture due to government patronage to justify the poor performance of the bourse over the last few years. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
